title: Cold rebuild: Validate a signup form
summary: Rebuild Validate a signup form from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Validate a signup form** in *Forms*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.explain: An empty age is allowed. `Number("abc")` is `NaN`, and `NaN >= 13` is false, so it fails. A missing email makes `data.email?.includes` give `undefined`, which is falsy.

steps.title: Rebuild Validate a signup form cold
prompt: Write `validateSignup(data: Record<string, string>)` returning an object of error messages (empty when valid):
- `email`: must contain one `@` with text on both sides and a `.` after the `@`: `"Enter a valid email"`
- `password`: at least 8 characters **and** at least one digit: `"Password needs 8+ characters and a number"`
- `confirm`: must equal password: `"Passwords do not match"`
Only include keys that have errors.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
